| [CASE-335](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-335.md) | A pilot coding of 30 public postmortems of software incidents and 10 Chemical Safety Board investigation reports, under a codebook fixed in advance, finds causes naming decisions above the engineering team in 2 of the postmortems and 7 of the reports, and action items above it in 4 and 9; one coder of the same model family as the claim it tests | A pilot of the study proposed as [CASE-293](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-293.md), run for [LEAD-119](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-119.md). Internal arm: 30 postmortems drawn at random (seed 119) from Dan Luu's public list of postmortems, each the organization's own account of its own incident. Independent arm: the 10 most recent completed investigations of the U.S. Chemical Safety Board with final reports. Each was coded for the highest organizational level whose decision a contributing cause names (0 unattributed to 5 outside authority, 3 being management decisions on priorities, staffing, schedules or cross-team policy) and the highest level an action item targets. Causes at level 3 or above: 2 of 30 postmortems (7%) against 7 of 10 reports; level 4 or above: 0 against 5. Action items at 3 or above: 4 of 30 (13%) against 9 of 10. Under the rule fixed before coding, [CLAIM-750](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-750.md)'s prediction holds in the pilot. The arms differ in domain (software outages against fatal or serious chemical accidents) as well as in who reviews, and there was one coder, of the same model family that wrote [CLAIM-750](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-750.md) and the codebook, knowing the prediction; the pilot is not independent. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CASE-411](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-411.md) | Eleven open-source successions coded from their public records, timing outside verdicts against the move: the earliest outside verdicts were arranged with the founders, every independent identity verdict found was made in the same act as the speaker's own move, recognition followed the maintainers where they moved wholesale and never the name except by reunion, and only one original line stopped producing | [CASE-223](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-223.md)'s design run on public records: eleven cases from the record's own list and the lead's brief (eight contested, two accepted, one unclassified), coded by rules written before the table, with 51 dated events each read from its source on 2026-11-23. The earliest outside verdicts on a successor were printed in its founders' own announcement (LibreOffice, Valkey) or were a foundation's taking it in (OpenTofu, Valkey, Forgejo). A response by an organization independent of the founders was found in four contested cases, after 0 to 1,189 days; three of the four were the speaker's announcement of its own move, and the one statement made before a move (Fedora's proposal to replace Redis) gave the licence as its only reason. The only verdict found dated before the move it decided is the Hudson community's rename vote (214 to 14), whose voters were the movers. Recognition went to the successor in both cases where the creator or the body of core maintainers moved (Jenkins, Libera Chat), split where part of the core moved (MariaDB, Valkey), and no successor took the original's name except io.js, by reunion. Only Hudson's line stopped producing, 2,294 days or fewer after the vote; the other originals still release. The public records cannot time verdicts apart from migration, which is [ARG-067](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-067.md)'s critical question.
